East Texas-South Texas.text: Spot cotton trading was active. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were lower. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. Forward contracting activity was inactive. Foreign mill inquiries were moderate, with mills from various countries seeking to take advantage of lower market levels. In East Texas, sunny but overcast conditions were interrupted by showers this week. Daytime highs ranged from the 70s to the 80s, with nighttime lows ranging from the 40s to the 70s. Rainfall activity produced accumulated moisture totals ranging from trace amounts up to one and one-quarter of an inch of rain. Producers completed post-harvest offseason preparations, shredding stalks and cultivating soil. Ginning operations continued to process modules stored on gin yards. Samples were transported to the classing office for classing services. In South Texas, overcast conditions dominated the skies throughout the region, with areas of the Upper Coast and Coastal Bend receiving rainfall early in the reporting period. Daytime high temperatures were in the 80s to the 90s, with nighttime low temperatures in the 60s to the 70s. Accumulated moisture totals ranged from trace amounts up to over two and one-quarter inches of moisture. Gins worked through modules on yards. Many are nearing the end of the season, but some expect to continue until late November. The Corpus Christi Classing Office reported a season total of 27.6 percent for color 31, 46.5 percent for leaf 3, staple averaging 36.9, mike averaging 43.4, strength averaging 31.5, and uniformity averaging 82.0 for week ending October 5.

West Texas-Kansas-Oklahoma.text: Spot cotton trading was slow. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were steady. Producer interest in forward contracting was light. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. Foreign mill inquiries were moderate, with mills from various countries seeking to take advantage of lower market levels. In Texas, daytime highs ranged from the mid-50s to the mid-80s, while nighttime temperatures fluctuated between the 30s and 60s. Light to moderate rainfall temporarily interrupted harvesting activities, with precipitation ranging from trace amounts to approximately two and one-half i nches of moisture. As fields dried and soils firmed under sunnier conditions, aerial applications of defoliants proceeded where needed. Stripper harvesting resumed by mid-week. Wet field conditions briefly hampered module transportation; however, ginning operations remained uninterrupted as gins worked through seed cotton supplies on gin yards. A few gins processed available module inventories and awaited additional module deliveries before resuming operations. Many sources reduced production estimates further. Recent rainfall delayed insurance adjustment activities. In Kansas, daytime temperatures ranged from the upper 50s to the mid-70s, while nighttime lows settled in the 30s and 50s. Several locations received up to two inches of moisture over multiple days. Harvesting activities were delayed until soils dried and firmed sufficiently to support field equipment. Ginning was underway at some locations, and modules accumulated slowly on gin yards, although not all gins were operating. Local sources reported pockets of irrigated fields yielding three and one-half to four bales per acre. In Oklahoma, harvest progress was slow after recent rainfall left soils soft and saturated. Water levels at Altus Lake increased slightly, which could benefit next year's crops. Daytime temperatures ranged from the mid-60s to the lower 80s, while overnight lows dipped into the 40s and 60s. Local experts reported fields were slow to defoliate, and regrowth remained a concern in some areas. Module transportation was hindered by soggy conditions. Warehouses received increasing numbers of bales as ginning operations advanced slowly, although not all gins had begun pressing bales.

Desert Southwest (DSW).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies and producer offerings were light. Demand was light. No forward contracting was reported during the period. Average local prices were lower. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Untimely rainfall was received in Safford, AZ, and Las Cruces, NM, during the final weekend of October. Daytime temperatures ranged from the 60s to the 80s. Nighttime lows ranged from the 40s to 60s. Total accumulated precipitation totals ranged from trace amounts up to one and one-quarter inches of rain in cotton-producing areas of the region. Saturated, muddy field conditions stalled progress in fields in Safford Valley. Producers waited for dry and open weather to allow soil to firm before returning to fields. The untimely rainfall may result in decreased yields, according to local sources. Ginning had begun in the region. Harvest continued in El Paso, TX.

San Joaquin Valley (SJV).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies and demand were light. No forward contracting or domestic mill activity was reported. Average local prices were lower. Foreign mill inquiries were light. In the SJV, open skies and sunny weather ruled during the period, with intermittent rainfall bringing some precipitation to the region. Daytime temperatures were in the 60s and 70s. Overnight lows were in the 40s. Accumulated rainfall totals measured from trace amounts up to over one-half of an inch of moisture. Weekend precipitation temporarily delayed harvest progression. However, as conditions allowed, producers resumed picking, moving quickly to make up for delays. Lower yields were reported in some fields, but overall producers have been pleased with the quality of the crop. Modules were transported to gins for pressing. Gins processed accumulated modules on gin yards.

American Pima (AP).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies were moderate. Demand was light. No forward contracting or domestic mill activity was reported. Average local spot prices were steady. Mill inquiries were moderate. Daytime highs in the Far West ranged from the 60s to the 80s, with nighttime lows in the 40s to the 60s. In the DSW, heavy weekend rains slowed harvest activities until fields could dry out and soils firm enough to support equipment. Flooding may result in decreased yields, according to local sources. Ginning began in the region. Harvesting activities continued in El Paso, TX. In the SJV, harvest was delayed as weekend rainstorms crossed the region, but picking resumed once suitable conditions returned. Pressing operations continued in the SJV.
